'''Karel Janeček''' (born 26 July 1973) is a Czech [[mathematician]], entrepreneur and philanthropist. He co-founded the financial company [[RSJ (company)|RSJ]] for [[algorithmic trading]].<ref>{{cite web |year=2023 |title=Karel Janeček |url=https://forbes.cz/lists/nc23/karel-janecek/ |access-date=30 August 2026 |website=Forbes Česko |language=cs}}</ref> He later became active in anti-corruption initiatives, philanthropy and electoral reform.

In 2011, Janeček co-founded the Anti-Corruption Endowment (''Nadační fond proti korupci'', NFPK), which supported whistleblowers and projects exposing corruption in public administration.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 August 2011 |title=Karel Janeček, zakladatel Nadačního fondu proti korupci |url=https://radiozurnal.rozhlas.cz/karel-janecek-zakladatel-nadacniho-fondu-proti-korupci-6331653 |access-date=30 August 2026 |website=Radiožurnál |publisher=[[Czech Radio]] |language=cs}}</ref> He also developed the [[D21 – Janeček method]], an alternative voting system.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jarabinský |first1=Ivan |last2=Oreský |first2=Jan |last3=Čech |first3=Prokop |year=2025 |title=D21 Method: A Path Toward Balanced Elections? |journal=Election Law Journal |volume=24 |issue=4 |pages=322–341 |doi=10.1089/elj.2024.0009|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Janeček was born in [[Plzeň]]. He graduated from the [[Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Charles University|Faculty of Mathematics and Physics]] of [[Charles University in Prague]] in the field of [[probability]] and [[mathematical statistics]].<ref name=biz>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20141014010206/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=115284062&privcapId=23712517|title=Executive Profile}}, ''[[Bloomberg Businessweek]]''</ref> He is an [[MBA]] in finance graduate of [[Bradley University]], [[Peoria, Illinois]], US, and a PhD graduate in the field of [[mathematical finance]] of [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]], US.<ref name=biz/>

==Academia==
From 2007 to 2013, Janeček lectured at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics of Charles University in Prague. He specializes in [[optimal control]] in [[mathematical finance]].<ref name=biz/>

Janeček has authored and co-authored several research articles in scientific journals in the area of applied [[stochastic calculus]], where his work has numerous citations,<ref name=biz/> such as "Optimal investment with high-watermark performance fee," ''SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization'', 2012; "Futures trading with transaction costs," ''Illinois Journal of Mathematics'', 2010; "Asymptotic analysis for optimal investment and consumption with transaction costs," ''Finance and Stochastics'', 2004; and others.
==Business==
From 1998 to 2000, Janeček worked as a mathematical analyst for the [[hedge fund]] Market Research Ltd.<ref>{{cite web |date=3 October 2011 |title=Rozhovor s Karlem Janečkem, podnikatelem a zakladatelem NFPK, nejen o korupci a obchodování |url=https://www.patria.cz/zpravodajstvi/1917542/rozhovor-s-karlem-janeckem-podnikatelem-a-zakladatelem-nfpk-nejen-o-korupci-a-obchodovani.html |access-date=30 August 2026 |website=Patria.cz |language=cs}}</ref> He founded the financial company [[RSJ (company)|RSJ]], which became known for [[algorithmic trading]] on international [[Derivative (finance)|derivatives]] markets. RSJ's core trading activity is [[Market maker|market making]], using automated trading systems to provide [[Market liquidity|liquidity]] by continuously placing buy and sell orders. The company focuses primarily on [[Futures contract|futures contracts]] and has traded on major exchanges in Europe, the United States and Asia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trading |url=https://www.rsj.com/en/securities/algorithmic-trading.html |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=RSJ Securities}}</ref>

RSJ's algorithmic trading became the main source of Janeček's wealth. He was for many years one of the company's largest shareholders but gradually reduced his involvement. In 2016, after having already left the company's management, he reduced his stake from 40% to 25%.<ref>{{cite news |last=Šenk |first=Michal |date=31 March 2016 |title=Janeček si nechal v RSJ jen čtvrtinový podíl. Větší váhu nyní mají šéfové IT a tradingu |url=https://archiv.hn.cz/c1-65228120-janecek-umensil-vliv-v-obchodnikovi-rsj |access-date=30 August 2026 |work=Hospodářské noviny |language=cs}}</ref>

==Anti-corruption campaign==
{{More|Corruption in the Czech Republic}}In 2011, Janeček co-founded the Anti-Corruption Endowment (''Nadační fond proti korupci'', NFPK) with businessman [[Stanislav Bernard]] and actor [[Jan Kraus (actor)|Jan Kraus]]. Janeček became chairman of the fund, which supported whistleblowers and projects aimed at exposing corruption in public administration.<ref name="irozhlas-profile">{{cite web |date=25 November 2022 |title=Kandidát na prezidenta Janeček: matematik a miliardář |url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/volby/profil-karel-janecek-kandidat-na-prezidenta-prezidentske-volby-2023_2211251100_jgr |access-date=30 August 2026 |website=iROZHLAS |language=cs}}</ref>

After President [[Václav Klaus]] announced a controversial amnesty in January 2013, Janeček financed a campaign calling for Klaus to be held accountable. A related petition gathered about 74,000 signatures, while 28 senators supported bringing a constitutional charge against Klaus.<ref name="LeMonde2013">{{cite news |last=Plichta |first=Martin |date=1 March 2013 |title=Karel Janecek, milliardaire et croisé anticorruption |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/international/article/2013/03/01/milliardaire-et-croise-anticorruption_1841515_3210.html |access-date=30 August 2026 |work=Le Monde |language=fr}}</ref> The Senate later approved the charge and submitted it to the [[Constitutional Court of the Czech Republic|Constitutional Court]].<ref>{{cite web |date=4 March 2013 |title=Senát schválil ústavní žalobu na Klause pro velezradu. Hlavně kvůli amnestii |url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/senat-schvalil-ustavni-zalobu-na-klause-pro-velezradu-hlavne-kvuli-amnestii_201303042130_sbartosova |access-date=30 August 2026 |website=iROZHLAS |language=cs}}</ref> The court discontinued the proceedings later that month without ruling on the merits, because Klaus's presidential term had already ended.<ref>{{cite web |date=27 March 2013 |title=Pl. ÚS 17/13: High Treason |url=https://www.usoud.cz/en/decisions/2013-03-27-pl-us-17-13-high-treason |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=Constitutional Court of the Czech Republic}}</ref>
==Political reform==
In 2013, Janeček introduced the [[D21 – Janeček method]], an electoral method in which voters can cast multiple positive votes and, in some versions, a negative vote. Janeček developed the system as an alternative intended to encourage broader consensus and reduce political polarization.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jarabinský |first1=Ivan |last2=Oreský |first2=Jan |last3=Čech |first3=Prokop |year=2025 |title=D21 Method: A Path Toward Balanced Elections? |journal=Election Law Journal |doi=10.1089/elj.2024.0009|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The method has mainly been used in [[participatory budgeting]] and other civic decision-making projects in the Czech Republic and abroad. Research has examined its effects on voter participation and electoral outcomes, although it has not been adopted for national parliamentary elections.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kukučková |first1=Soňa |last2=Poláchová |first2=Marie |year=2021 |title=The Impact of the D21 Method and Its Modification on Citizens' Participation in Participatory Budgeting: The Case of the Czech Republic |url=https://sjps.fsvucm.sk/index.php/sjps/article/view/241 |journal=Slovak Journal of Political Sciences |access-date=30 August 2026}}</ref>

== Philanthropy ==
In 2010, Janeček established a fund to support [[scientific research]] in the Czech Republic. In 2013, it became the Neuron Fund for Support of Science after additional private donors joined the initiative. The fund awards grants and prizes to Czech scientists and promotes private support for scientific research.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Boháček |first=Ivan |date=5 December 2013 |title=Neuron 2013: ceny za životní dílo a granty |url=https://vesmir.cz/cz/casopis/archiv-casopisu/2013/cislo-12/neuron-2013-ceny-za-zivotni-dilo-granty.html |journal=Vesmír |language=cs |access-date=30 August 2026}}</ref>

In November 2021, Neuron's scientific and governing boards ended their cooperation with Janeček after he criticized COVID-19 restrictions and the vaccination of children during the [[Český slavík]] awards. The fund said that some of his statements contradicted scientific evidence and distanced itself from his views.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lázňovský |first=Matouš |date=21 November 2021 |title=Další spolupráce není možná. Od Janečka se distancuje jím založený fond |url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/dalsi-spoluprace-neni-mozna-od-janecka-se-distancuje-jim-zalozeny-fond-181118 |access-date=30 August 2026 |work=Seznam Zprávy |language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=22 November 2021 |title=Nadační fond Neuron končí spolupráci s Janečkem kvůli proslovu na Slavících |url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/veda/3403596-nadacni-fond-neuron-konci-spolupraci-s-janeckem-kvuli-proslovu-na-slavicich |access-date=30 August 2026 |work=ČT24 |language=cs}}</ref>

==Gambling==
[[File:SBA_diskette.jpg|thumb|right|150px|{{center|<small>SBA [[floppy disk]]</small>}}]]

While studying in the United States in the 1990s, Janeček became interested in [[blackjack]] and [[card counting]] and played blackjack semi-professionally in American casinos. In 1995, he developed the Statistical Blackjack Analyzer (SBA), software for simulating blackjack strategies and analysing their expected returns and risk.<ref>{{cite news |date=13 July 2007 |title=Karel Janeček: Studium matematiky otvírá dveře do byznysu |url=https://archiv.hn.cz/c1-21618290-studium-matematiky-otvira-dvere-do-byznysu |access-date=31 August 2026 |work=Hospodářské noviny |language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |year=2022 |title=Karel Janeček |url=https://forbes.cz/lists/nc22/karel-janecek/ |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=Forbes Česko |language=cs}}</ref>

SBA was subsequently used by Don Schlesinger for simulations published in his book ''Blackjack Attack'', and specialist publications described SBA as one of the more advanced blackjack simulators of its period.<ref>{{cite book |last=Schlesinger |first=Don |title=Blackjack Attack: Playing the Pros' Way |publisher=RGE Publishing |year=2005 |edition=3rd}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Statistical Blackjack Analyzer |url=https://www.blackjackreview.com/wp/catalog/statistical-blackjack-analyzer/ |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=Blackjack Review}}</ref> Janeček also carried out mathematical analysis for [[Blackjack Switch]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wattenberger |first=Norm |title=Modern Blackjack |url=https://www.qfit.com/book/ModernBlackjackPage36.htm |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=QFIT}}</ref>

Janeček also wrote about mathematical approaches to blackjack wagering and risk. His article “Optimal Wagering and Betting”, published in ''Blackjack Review'' in 1998, examined methods for determining optimal betting strategies using simulations generated by SBA.<ref>{{cite web |last=Janeček |first=Karel |date=10 November 2024 |orig-date=1998 |title=Optimal Wagering and Betting |url=https://www.blackjackreview.com/wp/2024/11/10/optimal-wagering-and-betting/ |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=Blackjack Review}}</ref> He also contributed analyses and participated in technical discussions on [[Stanford Wong]]'s BJ21 blackjack community.<ref>{{cite web |last=Janeček |first=Karel |title=Certainty Equivalent Analysis |url=https://bj21.com/articles/advantage-play/certaintyequivalentanalysis |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=BJ21}}</ref>

==Presidential bid==
On 21 January 2022, Janeček announced that he would be running in the [[2023 Czech presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jeřábková |first=Dominika |date=2022-01-21 |title=Miliardář Janeček oznámil kandidaturu na prezidenta|language=cs |url=https://www.novinky.cz/clanek/volby-prezidenta-miliardar-janecek-oznamil-kandidaturu-na-prezidenta-40384701|access-date=2023-01-27 |website=novinky.cz}}</ref> He submitted 73,000 signatures, but this total was reduced following sample analysis to 48,000 (later the court labeled some of them as valid but he still failed to meet the criteria by 80 signatures), below the requirement.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dragoun|first=Radek|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/volby-soud-janecek-divis-rohanova/r~6a28ef247af411ed8b4e0cc47ab5f122/|title=Archy smyšlených podpisů, selhání úředníků. Soud ukázal na chyby vnitra i Janečka|language=cs|website=aktualne.cz|date=13 December 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Stuchlíková |first1=Lucie|last2=Rambousková|first2=Michaela|date=2022-11-25 |title=Matematik, betonový král a "obyčejný muž". Komu nevyšel sen o Hradu|language=cs |url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/volby-prezidentske-matematik-betonovy-kral-a-obycejny-muz-komu-nevysel-sen-o-hradu-220100|access-date=2023-01-27 |website=seznamzpravy.cz}}</ref> Janeček submitted a complaint to the [[Supreme Administrative Court of the Czech Republic|Supreme Administrative Court]].<ref name="Vnitro pustilo do boje o Hrad jen devět z 21 kandidátů, odmítlo třeba Janečka">{{cite web |title=Vnitro pustilo do boje o Hrad jen devět z 21 kandidátů, odmítlo třeba Janečka |url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/prezident-kandidati-nerudova-babis-pavel-fischer-volby-hlasy-hrad-cesko-2023.A221123_143631_domaci_klf |website=iDNES.cz |access-date=25 November 2022 |language=cs |date=25 November 2022 |archive-date=25 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221125120236/https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/prezident-kandidati-nerudova-babis-pavel-fischer-volby-hlasy-hrad-cesko-2023.A221123_143631_domaci_klf |url-status=live }}</ref> His complaint was rejected by the court on 13 December 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Diviše soud do voleb vrátil, Rohanovou vyřadil. Janeček se stížností neuspěl |url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/volby-budou-mit-devet-kandidatu-rohanovou-vystrida-divis-jan/r~bc40f6967ad911ed8980ac1f6b220ee8/ |website=Aktuálně.cz |access-date=19 December 2022 |language=cs |date=13 December 2022 |archive-date=19 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221219105144/https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/volby-budou-mit-devet-kandidatu-rohanovou-vystrida-divis-jan/r~bc40f6967ad911ed8980ac1f6b220ee8/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Janeček subsequently endorsed [[Petr Pavel]] in both rounds.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Wasserbauerová |first1=Terezie|last2=Svěrák|first2=Vojtěch |date=2023-01-13 |title=Janeček vyškrtl jméno generála Pavla, napsal vlastní. Lístek je platný|language=cs |url=https://www.idnes.cz/volby/prezidentske-volby-neuspesny-kandidat-janecek-volil-pavla.A230113_153906_volby_wass|access-date=2023-01-27 |website=idnes.cz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Vašinová |first=Jolana |date=2023-01-27 |title=Janeček se bez tužky neobešel ani tentokrát. Jméno Pavla přeškrtl, lístek platí|language=cs |url=https://www.idnes.cz/volby/petr-janecek-volby-druhe-kolo-propiska-hlasovaci-listek.A230127_150446_volby_vajo|access-date=2023-01-27 |website=idnes.cz}}</ref> On 3 February 2023 he submitted a complaint to the Supreme Administrative Court over the presidential election process.<ref>{{cite news|title=Janeček podal stížnost k NSS kvůli průběhu voleb|url=https://denikn.cz/minuta/1072957/|access-date=3 February 2023 |publisher=Deník N|website=denikn.cz|date=3 February 2023 |language=cs}}</ref> The Supreme Administrative Court rejected the challenge on 14 February 2023.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 February 2023 |title=Vol 40/2023-23 |url=https://vyhledavac.nssoud.cz/GetContent?ECLI=ECLI%3ACZ%3ANSS%3A2023%3AVol.40.2023.23 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=[[Supreme Administrative Court of the Czech Republic]] |language=cs}}</ref> The [[Constitutional Court of the Czech Republic|Constitutional Court]] rejected his subsequent complaint in May.<ref>{{cite web |date=9 May 2023 |title=Pl. ÚS 23/23 |url=https://nalus.usoud.cz/Search/GetText.aspx?sz=Pl-23-23_1 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=[[Constitutional Court of the Czech Republic]] |language=cs}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Janeček has two daughters from his first marriage to Michaela, and a son from his second marriage to Mariem.<ref name="idnes.2021.05.21"/> Since May 2017, he has been in a relationship with Lilia Khousnoutdinova, and they have a daughter<ref name="revue.idnes.2018.06.04">{{cite news |last=Herrmannová |first=Nela |date=4 June 2018 |title=Karel Janeček má se svou neoficiální ženou dceru, porod byl výjimečný |language=cs|trans-title=Karel Janeček has a daughter with his unofficial wife, the birth was exceptional |url=https://revue.idnes.cz/karel-janecek-lilia-khousnoutdinova-porod-dite-dcera-isabella-p6g-/lidicky.aspx?c=A180604_101834_lidicky_nh |work=Revue iDnes |location=Prague |access-date=1 December 2018}}</ref> and a son.<ref name="idnes.2021.05.21">{{Cite interview |last=Khousnoutdinova |first=Lilia |interviewer=Rastislav Zárodňanský |date=2021-05-21 |title=Janeček a Khousnoutdinova mají syna. Narodil se doma, pod skálou u řeky |language=cs |trans-title=Janeček and Khousnoutdinova have a son. He was born at home, under a rock by the river |url=https://www.idnes.cz/revue/spolecnost/karel-janecek-khousnoutdinova-porod-syn-karel-george-reka-dite.A210521_195030_lidicky_zar |access-date=24 May 2021 |website=iDNES.cz}}</ref> They got married first in a Buddhist wedding ceremony in Bhutan in 2017<ref name="revue.idnes.2018.06.04"/> and officially on 21 December 2021 in [[Prague]].<ref name="idnes.2021.12.21">{{Cite news |last=Šubrtová |first=Diana |date=2021-12-21 |title=Miliardář Janeček a matka jeho dvou dětí Khousnoutdinova se vzali|language=cs |url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/revue/vztahy-a-sex/lilia-khousnoutdinova-karel-janecek-svatba-vernost-matragi.A211220_122121_sex_sub|access-date=2022-12-27 |website=iDNES.cz}}</ref> He is a Buddhists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-15 |title=Meet the extrovert billionaire bidding to be Czech's next president |url=https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2022/02/15/meet-the-extrovert-billionaire-bidding-to-be-the-czech-republic-s-next-president |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=[[euronews]] |language=en}}</ref>
